1.explanation:
• TileLayer.js (WebGLTileLayerRenderer) drives each TileLayer to use a WebGL context via its base class.  
• Layer.js (WebGLLayerRenderer) instantiates a new WebGLHelper (and thus a new GL context) in prepareFrame for every layer.  
• Helper.js (WebGLHelper) wraps context creation but does not reuse or share contexts between instances.  
• webgl.js (getContext) always creates a fresh WebGLRenderingContext.  
To share a single WebGL context across multiple WebGL TileLayers, these files must be modified to centralize context creation (e.g. a shared WebGLHelper or context pool) rather than instantiating a new context per layer.
1.bug_scenario: An OpenLayers application using multiple WebGL-based TileLayers to render separate raster images is running into browser WebGL context limits (typically 16). Each WebGLTileLayerRenderer creates its own WebGL context via WebGLHelper, so with more than ~16 distinct TileLayers (e.g. separate GeoTIFFSources that cannot be merged) the browser evicts older contexts and layers begin to misrender or fail.
